title: Review: Particles, isotopes and relative atomic mass; Mass spectrometry of elements; Orbitals and electron configuration; Periodic table structure and blocks; Ionisation energies
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AS04#t3 term and clue written for the game; AS01#t1 term and clue written for the game; AS04#t1 term and clue written for the game; AS05#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AS01#N.15, AS02#N.6a, AS04#N.12a, AS05#N.7a, PT01#N.6, AS01#N.5a, AS02#N.8, AS04#N.9a, AS05#N.4a, PT01#N.12a, AS01#N.7a, AS02#N.13. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Atomic number
items.clue: The count of protons in a nucleus, symbol Z, which fixes the element.

items.label: Orbital
items.clue: A region around the nucleus where an electron is likely to be found; not a path.

items.label: Atomic radius
items.clue: The distance of the outer electron from the nucleus; it shrinks across a period.

questions.stem: Bromine's relative atomic mass is 79.90, almost exactly halfway between 79 and 81. What does this show?

options.text: Most bromine atoms are bromine-80, with 45 neutrons each.
Every bromine atom has the same mass, 79.90, between those of its two isotopes.
Bromine is a mixture of bromine-79 and bromine-81 atoms in roughly equal numbers.
Bromine's electrons add 0.90 to the mass of each bromine-79 atom.

questions.explanation: 50.7% ⁷⁹Br and 49.3% ⁸¹Br weight the two masses almost equally: (78.918 × 50.69 + 80.916 × 49.31) ÷ 100 = 79.90.

questions.stem: The mass spectrum of element E shows three peaks from singly charged atomic ions: m/z 24 (relative abundance 100), m/z 25 (relative abundance 12.7) and m/z 26 (relative abundance 13.9). What is the relative atomic mass of E, calculated from these data?
A ground-state phosphorus atom is [Ne] 3s² 3p³. Where are its three 3p electrons?

options.text: Together in one 3p orbital, which all three share.
On one circular orbit at a fixed distance from the nucleus.
Two paired in one 3p orbital, one in a second, the third left empty.
One in each of the three 3p orbitals, with parallel spins.

questions.explanation: Three equal-energy orbitals, three electrons: one each, spins parallel. Each electron is spread over its dumbbell-shaped region.

questions.stem: How does the first ionisation energy generally change across Period 3 from sodium to argon, and why?

options.text: It decreases, as the fixed pull of the nucleus is shared among more and more electrons.
It decreases, as the atoms get larger because more electrons are added along the period.
It increases, as atoms closer to a full outer shell resist losing any of their outer electrons.
It increases, as the nuclear charge rises while the outer electrons have similar shielding.

questions.explanation: Nuclear charge +11 to +18; the electron removed is in the third shell, with similar shielding. 496 → 1521 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: Germanium is in period 4, group 14. Which is the full electron configuration of a germanium atom?

options.text: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s² 4p²
1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d² 4s²
1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p²
1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p⁴

questions.explanation: Period 4, p-block: fill up to 4p. Group 14 gives 14 − 10 = 4 valence electrons, 4s² 4p². With the 3d¹⁰, the total is 32 electrons.

questions.stem: An ion X³⁺ contains 23 electrons and 30 neutrons. Which nuclear symbol represents this ion? (Each symbol is written with its superscript first and its subscript second.)

options.text: ⁵⁰₂₀X³⁺
⁵³₂₃X³⁺
⁵⁶₂₆X³⁺
²⁶₅₆X³⁺

questions.explanation: Protons = 23 + 3 = 26 = Z. Mass number = 26 + 30 = 56. (X is iron.)

questions.stem: Bromine atoms are about 50% ⁷⁹Br and 50% ⁸¹Br. Which describes the Br₂⁺ molecular-ion peaks in the mass spectrum of bromine?

options.text: m/z 158, 160 and 162, in the ratio 1 : 1 : 1
m/z 158 and 162 only, in the ratio 1 : 1
m/z 158, 160 and 162, in the ratio 9 : 6 : 1
m/z 158, 160 and 162, in the ratio 1 : 2 : 1

questions.explanation: ½ × ½ = ¼ for 158 and for 162; 2 × ½ × ½ = ½ for 160. Ratio 1 : 2 : 1.

questions.stem: An iron atom (Z = 26) has the condensed electron configuration [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s². How is an Fe²⁺ ion formed from this atom?

options.text: Two of the six 3d electrons are removed from the atom.
One 4s electron and one 3d electron are each removed.
Two electrons are added to the 3d sub-shell of the atom.
Both of the 4s electrons are removed from the atom.

questions.explanation: Transition metal atoms lose 4s electrons before 3d: [Ar] 3d⁶, 24 electrons.

questions.stem: Which equation represents the second ionisation energy of calcium?

options.text: Ca⁺(g) → Ca²⁺(g) + e⁻
Ca(g) → Ca²⁺(g) + 2e⁻
Ca⁺(aq) → Ca²⁺(aq) + e⁻
Ca(s) → Ca²⁺(g) + 2e⁻

questions.explanation: One mole of electrons removed from one mole of gaseous 1+ ions.

questions.stem: Beryllium, 1s² 2s², and helium, 1s², both have two electrons in their outer s sub-shell. Why is beryllium placed in group 2, but helium in group 18?

options.text: Beryllium is a solid and helium is a gas, and group 18 holds the gaseous elements.
Beryllium has four electrons and helium two, and the group number counts the total.
Beryllium's 2s² electrons are in a higher shell, so they are inner electrons, not valence electrons.
Beryllium's outer shell, n = 2, is far from full, while helium's n = 1 shell is full with just two.

questions.stem: Chlorine (atomic number 17) has isotopes with mass numbers 35 and 37. Pure samples of ³⁵Cl₂ gas and ³⁷Cl₂ gas are compared at the same temperature and pressure. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The ³⁷Cl₂ gas diffuses more slowly than ³⁵Cl₂.
The two gases diffuse at the same rate as each other.
The two gases undergo different chemical reactions.
The ³⁷Cl₂ molecules contain more electrons than ³⁵Cl₂.

questions.explanation: At the same temperature the heavier ³⁷Cl₂ molecules move more slowly on average. Diffusion rate is a physical property.

questions.stem: The mass spectrum of gallium shows two peaks from 1+ ions: m/z 69 (height 100) and m/z 71 (height 66.4). What is the relative atomic mass of gallium given by these data?
